before: Ruby can run instructions written in a script from top to bottom.
puts is a method, a named operation you can call, that displays a value and ends its line. Here it is called with text inside double quotes.
The quote marks identify text; they are not part of the displayed message.
These simple instructions need no semicolon. Each line below is a separate instruction.
Expected result: Moon then River on separate lines. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: A program is a set of instructions for a computer. Ruby reads these lines from top to bottom.
The quotes hold the words to show. They do not print as part of the words.
Show Moon and move to the next line.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
puts "Moon"
puts "River"
```
The output is `Moon`, then `River`. Moon appears first because its instruction comes first.
Trace the same two instructions in the opposite order.
